1	(b) The Clawback Amount shall be calculated by the Fund Administrator and verified by the Partnership's independent auditors in connection with the final audit of the Partnership's financial statements. The General Partner shall satisfy the Clawback Amount within ninety (90) days following the completion of the final accounting of the Partnership.
2	(c) The following senior professionals of the General Partner: Marcus Thornfield, Serena Hayworth, Viktor Osei, and Lydia Marchetti (collectively, the "Clawback Guarantors"), shall each provide a personal guarantee of the General Partner's clawback obligation under this Section 6.3, provided that the aggregate personal guarantee obligation of each Clawback Guarantor shall be limited to fifty percent (50%) of the after-tax Carried Interest received by such Clawback Guarantor (with taxes calculated at the Assumed Tax Rate). Such personal guarantees shall be in writing and delivered to the Partnership within thirty (30) days of the first distribution of Carried Interest to the General Partner.
3	(d) The General Partner may, in its discretion, establish an escrow account (the "Clawback Escrow") funded with a portion of each distribution of Carried Interest to satisfy potential clawback obligations. If the General Partner establishes a Clawback Escrow, not less than twenty-five percent (25%) of each distribution of Carried Interest to the General Partner shall be deposited into such escrow account and held until released in accordance with procedures determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC.
4	(e) For the avoidance of doubt, the clawback obligation is calculated on a net-of-tax basis, utilizing the Assumed Tax Rate. This methodology reflects the recognition that the General Partner and its principals will have paid taxes on distributions of Carried Interest and that requiring repayment on a gross (pre-tax) basis would require repayment of amounts that have already been paid to taxing authorities and cannot be recovered.
5	Section 6.4 — Withholding
6	(a) The General Partner is authorized to withhold from any distribution to any Partner, and to pay over to any federal, state, local, or foreign governmental authority, any amounts required to be withheld pursuant to applicable tax law. Any amounts so withheld shall be treated as having been distributed to the relevant Partner for all purposes under this Agreement, including for purposes of the distribution waterfall in Section 6.2.
7	(b) If the Partnership is required to pay any tax, fee, or assessment on behalf of or attributable to a Partner (including any withholding taxes), the General Partner may treat such payment as a distribution to such Partner or as a loan to such Partner, at the General Partner's election. If treated as a loan, such amount shall bear interest at the Default Interest Rate and shall be repaid from any subsequent distributions otherwise payable to such Partner.
8	Section 6.5 — Tax Distributions
9	Notwithstanding any other provision of this Article VI, the General Partner may, in its discretion, make distributions to the Partners in amounts sufficient to cover each Partner's estimated tax liabilities arising from allocations of taxable income from the Partnership (each such distribution, a "Tax Distribution"). Tax Distributions shall be calculated based on the highest combined marginal federal, state, and local income tax rate applicable to individuals resident in New York, New York (without regard to deductions, credits, exemptions, or other adjustments specific to any individual Partner). Tax Distributions shall be treated as advances on, and shall reduce, distributions otherwise payable to the receiving Partner under Section 6.2. If a Tax Distribution to any Partner exceeds the distributions that such Partner would otherwise be entitled to receive under Section 6.2 at the time of such Tax Distribution, such excess shall be treated as an advance and shall reduce subsequent distributions to such Partner. Tax Distributions shall be made at such times as the General Partner determines appropriate, including, without limitation, prior to the due dates for estimated tax payments.
10	Section 6.6 — Distribution in Kind
11	(a) The General Partner may, with the consent of the affected Limited Partners (which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, delayed, or conditioned), distribute Partnership assets in kind rather than in cash. Any asset distributed in kind shall be valued at its fair market value as of the date of distribution, as determined in good faith by the General Partner, and verified by the Fund Administrator.
12	(b) Each Partner receiving a distribution in kind shall bear such Partner's pro rata share of any costs or expenses associated with the distribution of such asset (including brokerage fees, transfer taxes, and legal fees). The General Partner shall provide each affected Partner with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice of any proposed distribution in kind, together with a description of the asset, the proposed valuation, and the basis for such valuation.
13	ARTICLE VII — MANAGEMENT FEE; EXPENSES
14	Section 7.1 — Management Fee
15	(a) During the Investment Period, the Management Company shall be entitled to receive a Management Fee equal to two percent (2.0%) per annum (200 basis points) of Aggregate Commitments, payable quarterly in advance on the first Business Day of each calendar quarter (each such quarterly payment being equal to one-half of one percent (0.5%) of Aggregate Commitments). The Management Fee shall commence on the date of the First Closing and shall be calculated based on the Aggregate Commitments as of the beginning of each calendar quarter.
16	(b) After the expiration or termination of the Investment Period, the Management Fee shall be equal to one and one-half percent (1.5%) per annum (150 basis points) of Invested Capital at cost (net of write-downs and write-offs to zero), payable quarterly in advance on the first Business Day of each calendar quarter. Invested Capital at cost shall be determined as of the beginning of each calendar quarter.
17	(c) The Management Fee for any partial calendar quarter shall be prorated on a daily basis (based on the actual number of days in such partial quarter divided by the actual number of days in the full calendar quarter).
18	(d) The Management Fee shall be calculated by reference to the Aggregate Commitments (as defined in Section 1.1 of this Agreement) and shall not be adjusted based on Capital Contributions drawn, distributions made, or borrowings under any Subscription Facility, Bridge Financing arrangement, or other credit facility of the Partnership. For the avoidance of doubt, amounts drawn under a Subscription Facility in lieu of Capital Calls shall not reduce the Aggregate Commitments for purposes of calculating the Management Fee, and the Management Fee shall continue to be payable on the full amount of Aggregate Commitments during the Investment Period regardless of the extent to which the Partnership utilizes a Subscription Facility or Bridge Financing.
19	(e) The Management Fee may be funded from Capital Contributions, from proceeds of any Subscription Facility, or from any other Partnership funds, as the General Partner may determine. If the General Partner elects to fund the Management Fee from a Capital Call, such Capital Call shall be made in accordance with Section 3.4.
20	(f) In the event of the termination of the Investment Period by reason of a Key Person Event under Section 9.3 (where the LPAC votes to permanently terminate the Investment Period) or the removal of the General Partner under Section 10.3, the Management Fee shall transition from the Aggregate Commitments base to the Invested Capital base as of the effective date of such termination or removal.
21	Section 7.2 — Organizational Expenses
22	The Partnership shall bear Organizational Expenses incurred in connection with the formation, organization, and offering of the Partnership, including legal fees, accounting fees, filing and registration fees, printing costs, regulatory costs, and other formation-related expenses, in an aggregate amount not to exceed Three Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars ($3,500,000). Any Organizational Expenses in excess of such amount shall be borne by the General Partner (or the Management Company) and shall not be charged to the Partnership or the Limited Partners. Organizational Expenses shall be amortized over the first sixty (60) months of the Fund Term for purposes of calculating Capital Account balances and financial reporting, unless the General Partner determines that a different amortization period is required under applicable accounting standards.
23	Section 7.3 — Partnership Expenses
24	The Partnership shall bear all reasonable and documented expenses incurred in connection with the operation, management, and administration of the Partnership, including, without limitation:
25	(a) Broken-Deal Expenses, subject to a cap of Two Million Dollars ($2,000,000) per proposed transaction. Any Broken-Deal Expenses in excess of such per-transaction cap shall be borne by the General Partner (or the Management Company) and shall not constitute Partnership Expenses;
26	(b) legal, accounting, audit, and tax preparation fees and expenses, including fees of Ironbark Audit Partners LLP (or any successor independent auditor selected by the General Partner) and fees of counsel to the Partnership;
27	(c) fees and expenses of Ridgeline Trust Company (or any successor fund administrator) in its capacity as Fund Administrator;
28	(d) custodial and banking fees and expenses;
29	(e) premiums for insurance maintained on behalf of the Partnership, including directors' and officers' liability insurance and errors and omissions insurance coverage;
30	(f) taxes, fees, and other governmental charges payable by the Partnership;
31	(g) costs and expenses incurred in connection with meetings of the LPAC, including travel expenses, meeting facilities, and reimbursements to LPAC members for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses;
32	(h) expenses incurred in connection with the acquisition, holding, monitoring, and disposition of Investments, including due diligence costs, appraisal fees, investment banking fees, brokerage commissions, and similar charges;
33	(i) indemnification obligations and expenses under Article XIII;
34	(j) costs of preparing and distributing financial reports, tax returns, and other communications to the Partners; and
35	(k) any other expenses that the General Partner determines in good faith are properly allocable to the Partnership and are not of the type customarily borne by the management company of a private equity fund.
36	For the avoidance of doubt, Partnership Expenses shall not include (i) the compensation of the General Partner's or the Management Company's employees, (ii) overhead expenses of the General Partner or the Management Company (including rent, office supplies, technology infrastructure, and similar costs), or (iii) placement agent fees payable in connection with the offering and sale of Interests (which shall be borne by the General Partner or the Management Company, as set forth in Section 7.7).
37	Section 7.4 — Fund-Level Borrowing; Bridge Financing
38	(a) The General Partner may cause the Partnership to incur Bridge Financing from time to time for the purpose of funding Investments or Partnership Expenses on a short-term basis in advance of Capital Contributions from the Partners. The aggregate principal amount of Bridge Financings outstanding at any time shall not exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of Aggregate Commitments (equal to $450,000,000 at the Target Fund Size). No single Bridge Financing shall remain outstanding for more than one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of the initial draw thereunder.
39	(b) Interest, fees, commitment fees, and other expenses incurred in connection with any Bridge Financing shall be Partnership Expenses and shall be borne by the Partnership.
40	(c) Amounts borrowed under a Bridge Financing shall be repaid from Capital Contributions made by the Partners in response to Capital Calls, from proceeds of Investments, or from other available Partnership funds.
41	Section 7.5 — Subscription Credit Facility
42	(a) The General Partner may cause the Partnership to enter into one or more Subscription Facilities, secured by the unfunded Capital Commitments of the Partners, in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed twenty-five percent (25%) of Aggregate Commitments (equal to $450,000,000 at the Target Fund Size). Each Partner hereby pledges, assigns, and grants a security interest in its Undrawn Commitment and the right to call such Partner's Capital Commitment as collateral for any Subscription Facility, and each Partner agrees to execute such documentation as may be reasonably required by the lender(s) under any such Subscription Facility to perfect such security interest.
43	(b) Amounts drawn under a Subscription Facility shall be treated as a temporary financing mechanism and shall not reduce the Capital Commitments of the Partners. Capital Contributions made by the Partners to repay borrowings under a Subscription Facility shall be treated as Capital Contributions for all purposes under this Agreement.
44	(c) Interest, fees, commitment fees, and other expenses incurred in connection with any Subscription Facility shall be Partnership Expenses and shall be borne by the Partnership.
45	(d) For the avoidance of doubt, the existence or utilization of any Subscription Facility shall not affect the calculation of the Management Fee, the Preferred Return, or any other economic provision of this Agreement. The Management Fee shall be based solely on Aggregate Commitments during the Investment Period as set forth in Section 7.1, and the use of a Subscription Facility in lieu of or in advance of Capital Calls shall not alter the amount, timing, or calculation of the Management Fee. Similarly, the use of a Subscription Facility shall not affect the calculation of the Preferred Return or the internal rate of return of any Partner for purposes of the distribution waterfall in Section 6.2, which shall be calculated based on the actual dates of Capital Contributions and distributions.
46	Section 7.6 — Fee Offsets
47	One hundred percent (100%) of any transaction fees, monitoring fees, directors' fees, advisory fees, consulting fees, break-up fees, or similar compensation received by the General Partner, the Management Company, or any of their respective Affiliates from Portfolio Companies or prospective Portfolio Companies (whether paid in cash or in kind) shall be applied to offset the Management Fee payable to the Management Company in subsequent quarters until the full amount has been offset. The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partners with a summary of all such fees and offsets as part of its quarterly reporting obligations under Article XV. For the avoidance of doubt, fees received by a Portfolio Company's independent directors who are not Affiliates of the General Partner shall not be subject to offset.
48	Section 7.7 — Placement Agent Disclosure
49	The General Partner hereby discloses that Calderbank Advisory Group has been retained as a non-exclusive placement agent for the Partnership in connection with the offer and sale of Interests to prospective Limited Partners. The Placement Agent is an independent third party and is not an Affiliate of the General Partner or the Management Company. Calderbank Advisory Group is entitled to a placement fee equal to one and one-half percent (1.5%) of the Capital Commitments of Limited Partners introduced to the Partnership by Calderbank Advisory Group. Placement agent fees are the obligation of the General Partner (or the Management Company) and shall not constitute Partnership Expenses. No placement agent fees shall be charged directly or indirectly to the Partnership or any Limited Partner. The General Partner shall provide each Limited Partner with information regarding (a) any placement agent fees paid in connection with such Limited Partner's Capital Commitment, and (b) any other material terms of the placement agent arrangement that are relevant to such Limited Partner, in each case upon written request by such Limited Partner. The General Partner shall also deliver to each Limited Partner, prior to or at the time of such Limited Partner's admission to the Partnership, a copy of the placement agent agreement (or a summary of its material terms) and a statement of any conflicts of interest related to the Placement Agent's engagement.
50	ARTICLE VIII — MANAGEMENT OF THE PARTNERSHIP
51	Section 8.1 — Authority of the General Partner
52	(a) The General Partner shall have full, exclusive, and irrevocable authority to manage and control the business and affairs of the Partnership and to do or cause to be done any and all acts and things deemed by the General Partner to be necessary, appropriate, or desirable to carry out the purposes of the Partnership, without any further act, vote, or approval of the Limited Partners, except as otherwise expressly required by this Agreement or by law.
53	(b) Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the General Partner shall have the authority, on behalf of the Partnership, to: (i) make, hold, monitor, and dispose of Investments; (ii) borrow money and grant security interests; (iii) enter into, amend, and terminate contracts and agreements; (iv) open and maintain bank accounts; (v) engage advisors, consultants, attorneys, accountants, and other service providers; (vi) bring, defend, and settle litigation; (vii) make elections and file returns for tax purposes; (viii) admit new Partners; (ix) make distributions; and (x) take any other action that the General Partner deems necessary or appropriate in connection with the business of the Partnership.
54	(c) No Limited Partner shall participate in the management or control of the Partnership's business, transact any business on behalf of the Partnership, or have any power or authority to bind the Partnership or to act on its behalf in any manner. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the exercise by a Limited Partner of any voting, consent, or approval right expressly granted to the Limited Partners under this Agreement shall not constitute participation in the management or control of the Partnership's business for purposes of DRULPA.
55	(d) Notwithstanding the foregoing, the General Partner shall not, without the prior approval of a Majority in Interest of Limited Partners, take any of the following actions: (i) amend this Agreement (except as provided in Section 17.1(a)); (ii) cause the Partnership to merge with, consolidate into, or convert to any other entity; (iii) cause the Aggregate Commitments to exceed the Hard Cap; or (iv) approve an Extension Period beyond the twelfth (12th) anniversary of the First Closing. In addition, certain actions require the approval or consultation of the LPAC, as set forth in Section 9.2.
56	Section 8.2 — Delegation
57	The General Partner may delegate any of its duties, powers, and authority under this Agreement to the Management Company (Thornfield Capital Partners, L.P.) or to any Affiliate of the General Partner, without the consent of the Limited Partners, and any such delegation shall not relieve the General Partner of its responsibilities and obligations under this Agreement. The General Partner may also engage third-party service providers to perform administrative, accounting, legal, and other functions on behalf of the Partnership.
58	Section 8.3 — Investment Decisions
59	All Investment decisions shall be made by the General Partner (or its delegee) in its sole discretion, subject to the Investment Restrictions set forth in Section 4.2 and the other provisions of this Agreement. No Limited Partner shall have any right to approve, reject, or participate in any Investment decision, except as expressly set forth in this Agreement (including with respect to Excused Investments under Section 3.6).
60	Section 8.4 — Standard of Care
61	The General Partner shall manage the Partnership in good faith, with the care that an ordinarily prudent person in a like position would exercise under similar circumstances, and in a manner that the General Partner reasonably believes to be in the best interests of the Partnership. The General Partner shall not be liable to the Partnership or any Partner for any act or omission taken in good faith and in accordance with the foregoing standard, subject to the exculpation and indemnification provisions of Article XIII.
62	Section 8.5 — Conflicts of Interest
63	(a) The General Partner and its Affiliates may manage other investment funds, accounts, and vehicles (including, without limitation, successor funds, parallel funds, and co-investment vehicles) that may have investment strategies that overlap with the Partnership. The General Partner shall allocate investment opportunities among the Partnership and any other fund or account in accordance with its allocation policy, which shall be designed to provide fair and equitable treatment to all participating funds and accounts.
64	(b) The General Partner shall present the Partnership's allocation policy to the LPAC for review within sixty (60) days of the First Closing and shall update the LPAC on any material changes to such policy.
65	(c) Transactions between the Partnership and the General Partner, the Management Company, or any Affiliate of the General Partner (including the purchase or sale of any asset, the provision of services, or any other arrangement) shall require the prior approval of the LPAC, unless such transaction is made on terms no less favorable to the Partnership than those that could be obtained in an arm's-length transaction with an unrelated third party.
66	(d) The General Partner shall disclose to the LPAC any material conflicts of interest that arise in connection with the management of the Partnership, and shall seek the LPAC's guidance or approval on the resolution of any such conflicts.
67	(e) The General Partner and its principals may serve on the board of directors (or equivalent governing body) of Portfolio Companies and may receive directors' fees or other compensation in connection therewith, subject to the fee offset provisions of Section 7.6.
68	Section 8.6 — Side Letters
69	The General Partner may enter into Side Letters or other writings with one or more Limited Partners that have the effect of supplementing, modifying, or waiving certain provisions of this Agreement with respect to such Limited Partner(s), including, without limitation, with respect to management fee rates, co-investment rights, reporting requirements, excuse rights, and other matters. No Side Letter shall (a) impose any additional obligation on the Partnership, the General Partner, or any other Partner without the consent of such other Person, or (b) adversely affect the rights of any other Partner under this Agreement without the consent of such other Partner. Side Letters shall be subject to the most-favored-nation provisions set forth in Section 8.7 and Section 16.2.
70	Section 8.7 — Most Favored Nation
71	(a) Disclosure. Within fifteen (15) Business Days following the Final Closing, the General Partner shall provide each Limited Partner that has a Capital Commitment equal to or greater than Seventy-Five Million Dollars ($75,000,000) (the "MFN Threshold") with copies of (or a summary of the material terms of) all Side Letters entered into between the General Partner and any other Limited Partner(s) in connection with the Partnership, redacted to remove identifying information regarding such other Limited Partner(s).
72	(b) Election. Within thirty (30) days following receipt of the Side Letter disclosure described in subsection (a) above, each eligible Limited Partner may elect (an "MFN Election") to receive the benefit of any or all terms contained in any single Side Letter granted to another Limited Partner whose Capital Commitment does not exceed one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the electing Limited Partner's Capital Commitment (the "Comparability Threshold"). An MFN Election shall be made by delivering written notice to the General Partner specifying the Side Letter whose terms the electing Limited Partner wishes to receive.
73	(c) Single Side Letter Requirement. An MFN Election shall be made with respect to all of the material terms of a single Side Letter (the "Single Side Letter Requirement"), and a Limited Partner may not elect individual provisions from multiple Side Letters. By way of example, if Side Letter A contains a fee reduction and a co-investment right, and Side Letter B contains an enhanced reporting right and a key person modification, an eligible Limited Partner must elect all of the material terms of either Side Letter A or Side Letter B, and may not elect the fee reduction from Side Letter A and the enhanced reporting from Side Letter B.
74	(d) Exclusions. Notwithstanding the foregoing, the following provisions shall be excluded from MFN Elections:
75	(i) terms granted to a Limited Partner solely to address specific legal, tax, or regulatory requirements applicable to such Limited Partner (including ERISA accommodations, tax treaty provisions, and government entity requirements);
76	(ii) terms that would, if extended to the electing Limited Partner, increase the obligations or reduce the rights of other Partners or of the Partnership;
77	(iii) LPAC membership; and
78	(iv) any terms that the General Partner reasonably determines are not capable of being replicated or extended to additional Limited Partners without material adverse consequences to the Partnership or other Partners.
79	(e) Effective Date. Any MFN Election shall become effective ten (10) Business Days following delivery of the election notice by the electing Limited Partner to the General Partner.
80	(f) Annual Re-Election. Following each anniversary of the Final Closing, if additional Side Letters have been entered into, the General Partner shall provide updated disclosure to eligible Limited Partners, and such Limited Partners shall have a thirty (30)-day election period to make or modify their MFN Elections in accordance with this Section 8.7.
81	Section 8.8 — Excuse/Exclusion Procedures
82	(a) A Limited Partner seeking to be excused from an Investment pursuant to Section 3.6 shall deliver written notice to the General Partner within five (5) Business Days of receiving the Capital Call Notice describing such Investment. Such notice shall set forth in reasonable detail the legal, regulatory, or binding policy basis for the excuse request, including a citation to the specific law, regulation, or binding policy at issue and, if requested by the General Partner, a written opinion of counsel confirming the applicability of such law, regulation, or binding policy to the requesting Limited Partner.
83	(b) The General Partner shall determine, in its reasonable discretion, whether the excuse request satisfies the requirements of Section 3.6(a), and shall notify the requesting Limited Partner of its determination within ten (10) Business Days of receiving the excuse request.
84	(c) If the General Partner determines that a Limited Partner is entitled to be excused, the Capital Commitment attributable to such Limited Partner's pro rata share of such Investment shall be reallocated among the remaining Partners (including the General Partner) on a pro rata basis in accordance with Section 3.6(c). The General Partner shall notify all Partners of such reallocation and shall adjust the Capital Call Notice accordingly.
85	(d) For purposes of the Investment Concentration Limit set forth in Section 4.2(a), the excused Limited Partner's Capital Commitment shall be excluded from Aggregate Commitments in calculating the remaining Partners' exposure to such Investment. The Investment Concentration Limit shall be applied to the adjusted Aggregate Commitments (i.e., Aggregate Commitments less the excused Limited Partner's Capital Commitment) with respect to such Investment, but the unadjusted Aggregate Commitments shall continue to apply for all other purposes under this Agreement.
86	(e) No Limited Partner shall be excused from Investments representing more than fifteen percent (15%) of Aggregate Commitments in the aggregate during the Fund Term without the prior written consent of the General Partner. If a Limited Partner exceeds this limitation, the General Partner may, in its discretion, require such Limited Partner to participate in subsequent Investments or may reduce such Limited Partner's Capital Commitment accordingly.
87	(f) The excuse or exclusion of a Limited Partner from an Investment shall not affect such Limited Partner's obligations with respect to other Investments or its general obligations under this Agreement, including its obligation to fund Capital Calls for Management Fees, Partnership Expenses, and Organizational Expenses.
88	ARTICLE IX — LIMITED PARTNER ADVISORY COMMITTEE; KEY PERSONS
89	Section 9.1 — Establishment and Composition of the LPAC
90	(a) The General Partner shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the "LPAC") consisting of seven (7) members (or such other number as the General Partner may determine from time to time). The initial LPAC shall be established within sixty (60) days of the First Closing.
91	(b) LPAC members shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the Limited Partners (or their designated representatives). In making such appointments, the General Partner shall endeavor to include representation from different categories of Limited Partners, including public pension funds, corporate pension funds, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, endowments and foundations, and fund-of-funds, to the extent that such investor types are represented among the Limited Partners.
92	(c) LPAC members shall serve at the pleasure of the General Partner and may be removed or replaced by the General Partner at any time for any reason or for no reason. A Limited Partner that ceases to be a Limited Partner (by reason of transfer or withdrawal) shall be automatically removed from the LPAC.

(d) LPAC members shall serve without compensation from the Partnership, but shall be reimbursed for reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in connection with LPAC meetings and LPAC-related activities. Such reimbursement shall constitute a Partnership Expense.
(e) LPAC membership shall not be subject to MFN Elections under Section 8.7 or Section 16.2.
Section 9.2 — LPAC Meetings and Functions
(a) The LPAC shall meet at least once per year (in person or by videoconference), and additionally at such times as may be requested by the General Partner or by a majority of the LPAC members. LPAC meetings shall be convened by the General Partner upon at least fifteen (15) Business Days' prior written notice to the LPAC members, which notice shall include a reasonably detailed agenda for such meeting.
(b) The functions of the LPAC shall include:
(i) reviewing and approving conflicts of interest transactions between the Partnership and the General Partner, the Management Company, or any of their respective Affiliates, as contemplated by Section 8.5(c);
(ii) reviewing valuations of Portfolio Company Investments on a quarterly basis and providing input on the valuation methodology employed by the General Partner and the Fund Administrator;
(iii) approving any extension of the Fund Term beyond the tenth (10th) anniversary of the First Closing, as contemplated by Section 2.6;
(iv) reviewing and approving the Co-Investment Allocation Policy, as contemplated by Section 9.6;
(v) consulting with the General Partner on proposed amendments to this Agreement and providing recommendations thereon;
(vi) voting on the reinstatement, termination, or wind-down of the Investment Period following a Key Person Event, as contemplated by Section 9.3(c);
(vii) approving any replacement Key Person designated by the General Partner pursuant to Section 9.5; and
(viii) such other matters as the General Partner may refer to the LPAC from time to time.
(c) The LPAC shall act in an advisory capacity only. LPAC members shall not owe fiduciary duties to any Limited Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC. No LPAC member shall be liable to any Limited Partner, the Partnership, or the General Partner for any action taken or omitted in good faith in its capacity as an LPAC member.
(d) Determinations of the LPAC shall be made by a majority vote of the LPAC members present (in person, by telephone, or by videoconference) at a duly convened meeting at which a quorum is present. A quorum for any LPAC meeting shall consist of a majority of the then-serving LPAC members. LPAC members may participate by proxy, provided that a written proxy is delivered to the General Partner prior to the relevant meeting. Determinations of the LPAC may also be made by written consent signed by a majority of the LPAC members, without a meeting.
Section 9.3 — Key Person Event
(a) A "Key Person Event" shall occur if either (i) Marcus Thornfield (Founder and Managing Partner) or (ii) Serena Hayworth (Partner and Co-Chief Investment Officer) ceases to devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership and the General Partner, other than as a result of (A) death or permanent disability (in which case a Key Person Event shall be deemed to have occurred), or (B) a temporary leave of absence of no more than ninety (90) consecutive days (in which case a Key Person Event shall not be deemed to have occurred, unless such leave is extended beyond ninety (90) consecutive days). For the avoidance of doubt, a Key Person Event shall be triggered by the departure of either Key Person; it is not necessary that both Key Persons cease their involvement for a Key Person Event to occur.
(b) Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the Investment Period shall be automatically suspended (the "Key Person Suspension"). During a Key Person Suspension:
(i) No new Investments shall be made by the Partnership, other than follow-on Investments in existing Portfolio Companies that were approved by the General Partner's investment committee prior to the date of the Key Person Event;
(ii) Capital Calls shall be limited to (A) funding existing binding commitments made prior to the Key Person Event, (B) making follow-on Investments permitted under clause (i) above, and (C) paying Management Fees, Partnership Expenses, and other obligations of the Partnership; and
(iii) The General Partner shall promptly (and in any event within five (5) Business Days of the Key Person Event) notify all Limited Partners and the LPAC in writing of the occurrence of the Key Person Event and the commencement of the Key Person Suspension.
(c) Within ninety (90) days following the occurrence of a Key Person Event, the LPAC shall convene a meeting (which may be held in person, by telephone, or by videoconference) and shall vote on one of the following courses of action:
(i) Reinstatement. Reinstate the Investment Period, upon such conditions as the LPAC deems appropriate (which may include the designation of a replacement Key Person in accordance with Section 9.5, the imposition of additional investment restrictions, or other conditions);
(ii) Termination. Permanently terminate the Investment Period, in which case the General Partner shall manage the Partnership's existing portfolio and wind down the Partnership in an orderly manner in accordance with Article XI; or
(iii) Wind-Down. Commence an orderly wind-down of the Partnership (which may be in addition to or in lieu of a permanent termination of the Investment Period), in which case the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to dispose of the Partnership's remaining Investments and distribute the proceeds to the Partners in accordance with Article VI.
(d) A vote under Section 9.3(c) shall require a majority of the LPAC members. If the LPAC fails to take action within the ninety (90)-day period, the Key Person Suspension shall continue until the LPAC convenes and votes on one of the foregoing courses of action.
Section 9.4 — Devotion of Time
Each Key Person shall devote substantially all of his or her business time and attention to the affairs of the Partnership and the General Partner. The foregoing shall not be deemed to prohibit a Key Person from (a) serving on the boards of directors of Portfolio Companies, (b) engaging in charitable, civic, educational, or professional activities, (c) managing personal investments, or (d) engaging in such other activities as do not materially interfere with such Key Person's obligations to the Partnership, in each case provided that such activities are disclosed to the LPAC in connection with its annual meeting.
Section 9.5 — Replacement of Key Persons
If a Key Person Event is cured by the designation of a replacement Key Person approved by the LPAC (by majority vote), the Investment Period shall resume as of the date of such LPAC approval. A proposed replacement Key Person must be a senior professional of the General Partner (or the Management Company) with at least ten (10) years of experience in private equity investing and must be approved by a majority vote of the LPAC. Upon approval, Exhibit D shall be amended to include the replacement Key Person, and such amendment shall be delivered to all Limited Partners.
Section 9.6 — Co-Investment Allocation Policy
(a) Within ninety (90) days of the First Closing, the General Partner shall adopt a Co-Investment Allocation Policy and submit it to the LPAC for review and approval. The LPAC shall review and vote on the proposed Co-Investment Allocation Policy within thirty (30) days of receipt. If the LPAC does not approve the proposed policy, the General Partner shall revise the policy taking into account the LPAC's comments and resubmit it for approval.
(b) The Co-Investment Allocation Policy shall set forth the criteria and procedures for allocating Co-Investment opportunities among Limited Partners, the General Partner, and their respective Affiliates, including the factors to be considered in making allocations. Such factors may include, without limitation: (i) Capital Commitment size, (ii) prior participation in Co-Investments, (iii) available co-investment capacity and speed of execution, (iv) diversification considerations, (v) strategic value to the Portfolio Company, and (vi) such other factors as the General Partner deems relevant.
(c) Any material amendment to the Co-Investment Allocation Policy shall require the approval of a majority of the LPAC members.
(d) Subject to the Co-Investment Allocation Policy and any Side Letter commitments, the General Partner shall have discretion in the allocation of specific Co-Investment opportunities to individual Limited Partners or their Affiliates. The General Partner shall report to the LPAC at least annually on Co-Investment activity, including a summary of the opportunities offered, participation rates, and aggregate amounts co-invested by Limited Partners.
ARTICLE X — REMOVAL OF THE GENERAL PARTNER
Section 10.1 — General
The General Partner may be removed only in accordance with the provisions of this Article X. No Limited Partner acting individually shall have the right to remove the General Partner. The removal of the General Partner shall not cause the dissolution of the Partnership unless a successor general partner is not appointed within the time period specified herein.
Section 10.2 — Voluntary Withdrawal
The General Partner may voluntarily withdraw from the Partnership upon not less than one hundred eighty (180) days' prior written notice to all Limited Partners, subject to the prior approval of a Majority in Interest of Limited Partners for the appointment of a successor general partner. Upon such withdrawal, the withdrawing General Partner shall cooperate in an orderly transition and shall continue to serve as General Partner until a successor is duly appointed and qualified.
Section 10.3 — Removal
(a) No-Fault Removal. The General Partner may be removed without Cause by Limited Partners holding not less than seventy-five percent (75%) in Interest of the Limited Partners (excluding the General Partner and its Affiliates) (a "No-Fault Removal"). A No-Fault Removal shall be effected by the delivery of a written notice signed by the requisite Limited Partners to the General Partner, which notice shall specify the effective date of the removal (which shall not be less than sixty (60) days after the date of such notice). Upon a No-Fault Removal:
(i) the Investment Period shall immediately terminate as of the effective date of removal;
(ii) a successor general partner shall be appointed by Limited Partners holding a Majority in Interest of the Limited Partners (excluding the removed General Partner and its Affiliates), and such successor general partner shall be admitted to the Partnership in accordance with the procedures set forth in Section 10.4;
(iii) the removed General Partner shall be entitled to continue to receive Carried Interest with respect to Investments made, and commitments entered into, prior to the effective date of removal, subject to and in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.2 and the clawback provisions of Section 6.3, but shall not be entitled to Carried Interest with respect to any Investments made after the effective date of removal;
(iv) the Management Fee shall cease to accrue as of the effective date of removal; and
(v) the removed General Partner shall retain its indemnification and exculpation rights under Article XIII with respect to actions taken or omitted prior to the effective date of removal.
(b) For-Cause Removal. The General Partner may be removed for Cause by Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) in Interest of the Limited Partners (excluding the General Partner and its Affiliates) (a "For-Cause Removal"). "Cause" shall mean:
(i) fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence by the General Partner (or any of its principals acting on behalf of the General Partner) in the performance of its duties under this Agreement;
(ii) a material breach of this Agreement by the General Partner that remains uncured for sixty (60) days following written notice of such breach from Limited Partners holding at least twenty-five percent (25%) in Interest to the General Partner;
(iii) the conviction of any principal of the General Partner (including Marcus Thornfield, Serena Hayworth, Viktor Osei, or Lydia Marchetti) of a felony involving moral turpitude; or
(iv) the bankruptcy, insolvency, or dissolution of the General Partner (other than a dissolution carried out for the purpose of a reorganization in which a successor entity assumes all of the General Partner's obligations under this Agreement).
A For-Cause Removal shall be effected by the delivery of a written notice signed by the requisite Limited Partners to the General Partner, which notice shall specify the Cause for removal and the effective date of the removal (which shall not be less than thirty (30) days after the date of such notice, during which period the General Partner may cure any curable Cause). Upon a For-Cause Removal:
(x) the Investment Period shall immediately terminate as of the effective date of removal;
(y) the removed General Partner shall forfeit all unpaid Carried Interest (i.e., Carried Interest that has been allocated but not yet distributed), but shall retain Carried Interest previously distributed, subject to the clawback provisions of Section 6.3; and
(z) a successor general partner shall be appointed by Limited Partners holding a Majority in Interest of the Limited Partners (excluding the removed General Partner and its Affiliates).
(c) For purposes of this Section 10.3, "in Interest" means measured by the aggregate Capital Commitments of the relevant Limited Partners as a proportion of the total Capital Commitments of all Limited Partners (excluding the General Partner and its Affiliates, and excluding any Defaulting Limited Partners).
Section 10.4 — Transition Provisions
(a) Upon the removal or withdrawal of the General Partner, the removed or withdrawing General Partner shall cooperate fully in an orderly transition, including by (i) delivering to the successor general partner all books, records, files, and documents relating to the Partnership and its Investments; (ii) assigning to the successor general partner (or the Partnership, as directed by the successor general partner) all agreements, contracts, and arrangements to which the General Partner is a party on behalf of the Partnership, to the extent assignable; (iii) providing reasonable access to the General Partner's personnel to facilitate the transition; and (iv) executing such documents and instruments as may be reasonably necessary to effectuate the transfer of management authority to the successor general partner.
(b) The removed or withdrawing General Partner shall retain its indemnification and exculpation rights under Article XIII with respect to actions taken or omitted during the period in which it served as General Partner.
(c) The costs and expenses of the transition (including legal fees and expenses) shall be borne by the Partnership as Partnership Expenses, except that expenses incurred solely for the benefit of the removed or withdrawing General Partner (such as legal fees in connection with the negotiation of the removal terms) shall be borne by the removed or withdrawing General Partner.
ARTICLE XI — DISSOLUTION AND WINDING UP
Section 11.1 — Events of Dissolution
The Partnership shall be dissolved upon the earliest to occur of any of the following events:
(a) the expiration of the Fund Term (including any Extension Periods);
(b) the vote of Limited Partners holding at least eighty percent (80%) in Interest of the Limited Partners (excluding the General Partner and its Affiliates) to dissolve the Partnership;
(c) the removal or withdrawal of the General Partner and the failure to appoint a successor general partner within one hundred eighty (180) days following such removal or withdrawal;
(d) the entry of a judicial decree of dissolution under Section 17-802 of DRULPA; or
(e) the determination by the General Partner, in its reasonable discretion, that dissolution is necessary or appropriate, including by reason of a change in law that makes the continued operation of the Partnership impractical or by reason of the Partnership having disposed of all or substantially all of its Investments.
Section 11.2 — Winding Up
(a) Upon dissolution, the General Partner (or, if there is no General Partner, a liquidating trustee appointed by a Majority in Interest of the Limited Partners) shall proceed to wind up the affairs of the Partnership and liquidate the Partnership's assets in an orderly manner designed to maximize value for the Partners.
(b) During the winding up period, the General Partner (or the liquidating trustee) shall (i) apply the proceeds of liquidation to satisfy the liabilities and obligations of the Partnership (including obligations to creditors and Partners who are creditors, to the extent otherwise permitted by law); (ii) establish reasonable reserves for contingent or unliquidated liabilities and obligations of the Partnership; and (iii) distribute the remaining proceeds to the Partners in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.2.
(c) The General Partner (or the liquidating trustee) shall provide the Limited Partners with periodic reports on the progress of the winding up, including an accounting of all asset dispositions and distributions.
(d) The winding up of the Partnership shall be completed as expeditiously as practicable, but the General Partner shall not be required to dispose of any asset at a price or on terms that the General Partner determines, in good faith, to be unfavorable to the Partnership.
Section 11.3 — Distributions Upon Dissolution
Distributions upon dissolution shall be made in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.2, after satisfaction of (or the establishment of reserves for) all liabilities and obligations of the Partnership. A final accounting shall be prepared and provided to all Partners, and any Clawback Amount payable by the General Partner pursuant to Section 6.3 shall be settled in connection with such final accounting.
Section 11.4 — Cancellation of Certificate
Upon the completion of the winding up and the distribution of all Partnership assets, the General Partner (or the liquidating trustee) shall cause the Certificate of Limited Partnership to be cancelled by filing a certificate of cancellation with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware in accordance with DRULPA.
ARTICLE XII — TRANSFERS
Section 12.1 — Restrictions on Transfer
(a) No Limited Partner may sell, assign, transfer, pledge, hypothecate, encumber, or otherwise dispose of (each, a "Transfer") all or any portion of its Interest in the Partnership without the prior written consent of the General Partner, which consent may be withheld by the General Partner in its sole and absolute discretion.
(b) In determining whether to consent to a proposed Transfer, the General Partner may take into account such factors as it deems relevant, including, without limitation: (i) the potential tax consequences to the Partnership and the Partners (including the risk of a "technical termination" under Section 708(b) of the Code or a reduction in the basis of Partnership assets); (ii) regulatory implications (including ERISA considerations and securities law compliance); (iii) the identity, reputation, financial condition, and sophistication of the proposed transferee; (iv) the impact on the Partnership's compliance with the benefit plan investor threshold set forth in Section 20.9; and (v) any other considerations that the General Partner deems relevant to the interests of the Partnership and the Partners.
(c) Any purported Transfer that is not made in compliance with this Article XII shall be void and of no force or effect, and the Partnership shall not recognize or be bound by any such Transfer.
Section 12.2 — Permitted Transfers
Notwithstanding Section 12.1, the following Transfers shall not require the consent of the General Partner (each, a "Permitted Transfer"):
(a) a Transfer by a Limited Partner to a Controlled Affiliate of such Limited Partner, provided that such Limited Partner (or an Affiliate thereof that controls the transferee) retains the economic risk and investment decision-making authority with respect to the transferred Interest, and provided further that the transferor delivers written notice to the General Partner at least fifteen (15) Business Days prior to the effective date of such Transfer;
(b) a Transfer by operation of law (including a transfer by will or intestacy, or a transfer resulting from a merger, consolidation, or reorganization of a Limited Partner), provided that the transferee meets the requirements of Section 12.3; and
(c) a Transfer to the General Partner or to a Person designated by the General Partner in connection with the exercise of default remedies under Section 3.5.
Section 12.3 — Conditions to Transfer
Any Transfer of an Interest (whether or not consent is required) shall be subject to the following conditions:
(a) The transferor shall deliver written notice to the General Partner at least thirty (30) days prior to the proposed effective date of the Transfer, specifying the identity of the proposed transferee, the amount of the Interest to be transferred, the proposed terms of the Transfer, and such other information as the General Partner may reasonably request;
(b) The proposed transferee shall execute and deliver to the General Partner an assumption agreement in form and substance satisfactory to the General Partner, pursuant to which the transferee assumes all obligations of the transferor under this Agreement with respect to the transferred Interest (substantially in the form attached hereto as Exhibit C);
(c) The transferor shall deliver to the General Partner, at its sole expense, such legal opinions as the General Partner may reasonably request, including opinions relating to (i) the exemption of the Transfer from the registration requirements of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and applicable state securities laws, (ii) the tax consequences of the Transfer to the Partnership and the Partners, and (iii) the ERISA status of the proposed transferee;
(d) The transferor shall pay all costs and expenses of the General Partner and the Partnership incurred in connection with the Transfer, including reasonable attorneys' fees; and
(e) The Transfer shall not violate any applicable law, regulation, or order, and shall not result in the Partnership being required to register as an investment company under the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended.
Section 12.4 — Effect of Transfer
Upon the completion of a Transfer in compliance with this Article XII, the transferee shall be admitted as a substituted Limited Partner and shall be bound by all terms and conditions of this Agreement (including any Side Letter to which the transferor was a party, unless otherwise agreed by the General Partner). The transferor shall be released from all future obligations under this Agreement with respect to the transferred Interest (including the obligation to fund Capital Calls attributable to the transferred Interest), except that the transferor shall remain liable for (a) any clawback obligation attributable to periods prior to the Transfer and (b) any indemnification obligation arising from actions or events occurring prior to the Transfer.
ARTICLE XIII — EXCULPATION AND INDEMNIFICATION
Section 13.1 — Exculpation
No Indemnified Person (as defined below) shall be liable to the Partnership, any Partner, or any other Person for any loss, damage, liability, or expense (including lost profits, diminution in value, or consequential damages) arising from or relating to any act or omission taken or suffered by such Indemnified Person in connection with the business and affairs of the Partnership, unless such loss, damage, liability, or expense resulted from such Indemnified Person's (a) fraud, (b) willful misconduct, (c) gross negligence, or (d) material breach of this Agreement. "Indemnified Person" means the General Partner and its Affiliates, and each of their respective officers, directors, employees, members, partners, managers, agents, and representatives. No Indemnified Person shall be liable to the Partnership or any Partner for any error of judgment or mistake of fact or law, or for any act or omission reasonably believed by such Indemnified Person to have been authorized by or within the scope of authority conferred under this Agreement, so long as such act or omission does not constitute fraud, willful misconduct, gross negligence, or a material breach of this Agreement.

2	The Partnership shall indemnify and hold harmless each Indemnified Person from and against any and all losses, claims, damages, liabilities, expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees, costs of investigation, and amounts paid in settlement), judgments, fines, penalties, and amounts paid in settlement arising from or relating to any action, suit, proceeding (whether civil, criminal, administrative, investigative, or otherwise), demand, assessment, or claim (each, a "Proceeding") that is brought, asserted, or threatened against such Indemnified Person in connection with the business and affairs of the Partnership, provided that (a) such Indemnified Person acted in good faith and in a manner such Indemnified Person reasonably believed to be in, or not opposed to, the best interests of the Partnership, and (b) such loss, claim, damage, liability, or expense did not result from such Indemnified Person's fraud, willful misconduct, or gross negligence.
