3	Section 13.3 — Advancement of Expenses
4	The Partnership shall advance to each Indemnified Person reasonable attorneys' fees and expenses incurred by such Indemnified Person in connection with any Proceeding in advance of the final disposition of such Proceeding, upon receipt of an undertaking by or on behalf of such Indemnified Person to repay such amounts if it shall be ultimately determined that such Indemnified Person is not entitled to indemnification under Section 13.2. The undertaking to repay shall be unsecured and shall be accepted without regard to the financial ability of the Indemnified Person to make repayment.
5	Section 13.4 — Insurance
6	The Partnership may purchase and maintain insurance on behalf of the Indemnified Persons and the Partnership against any liability, loss, or expense, whether or not the Partnership would have the power to indemnify such Persons against such liability, loss, or expense under this Article XIII. The cost of such insurance shall be a Partnership Expense. The General Partner shall select the insurance coverage, carriers, and policy terms in its discretion, and shall provide the LPAC with a summary of insurance coverage upon request.
7	ARTICLE XIV — CONFIDENTIALITY
8	Section 14.1 — Definition of Confidential Information
9	"Confidential Information" means all information relating to the Partnership, its Investments, Portfolio Companies, Limited Partners, and their respective financial, operational, and business affairs, including, without limitation, (a) the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Side Letters, (b) the Capital Commitments, Capital Account balances, and investment records of the Partners, (c) all reports, financial statements, valuations, and communications provided by or on behalf of the General Partner to the Partners, (d) all information relating to the investment strategy, pipeline, processes, and decision-making of the General Partner and the Management Company, (e) all information relating to the business, operations, financial condition, and prospects of any Portfolio Company, and (f) all other non-public information provided to or obtained by the Partners in connection with the Partnership. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Confidential Information shall not include information that (i) is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a breach of this Agreement, (ii) was in the receiving party's possession (as evidenced by written records) prior to disclosure by or on behalf of the Partnership, (iii) is independently developed by the receiving party without use of or reference to any Confidential Information, or (iv) is received from a third party who is not, to the knowledge of the receiving party, bound by any obligation of confidentiality with respect to such information.
10	Section 14.2 — Confidentiality Obligations
11	Each Partner agrees to maintain the confidentiality of all Confidential Information and shall not disclose, publish, or disseminate Confidential Information to any Person, except:
12	(a) to such Partner's Affiliates, officers, directors, employees, trustees, beneficiaries, partners, members, shareholders, advisors (including legal, accounting, financial, and tax advisors), consultants, and agents (collectively, "Authorized Recipients") who have a reasonable need to know such information in connection with such Partner's investment in the Partnership and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article XIV (and each Partner shall be responsible for any breach of such obligations by its Authorized Recipients);
13	(b) as required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, including, without limitation, any judicial, administrative, or governmental order, decree, subpoena, or request;
14	(c) to any governmental, regulatory, or self-regulatory authority having jurisdiction over such Partner, in connection with routine examinations, supervisory inquiries, or regulatory filings;
15	(d) in connection with a proposed Transfer of such Partner's Interest, to a bona fide prospective transferee that has entered into a written confidentiality agreement in form and substance reasonably acceptable to the General Partner;
16	(e) in connection with a proposed commitment by a prospective limited partner to a successor fund managed by the General Partner or its Affiliates, to the extent that such disclosure is approved in advance by the General Partner; and
17	(f) with the prior written consent of the General Partner.
18	Each Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that any disclosure of Confidential Information pursuant to clauses (b) and (c) above is limited to the minimum amount of information required to satisfy the applicable legal, regulatory, or judicial requirement.
19	Section 14.3 — Duration of Confidentiality Obligations
20	The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article XIV shall survive the dissolution and liquidation of the Partnership and the withdrawal, removal, or Transfer of any Partner's Interest for a period of three (3) years following the occurrence of such event. Following the expiration of such three (3)-year period, each Partner shall continue to maintain the confidentiality of Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law.
21	Section 14.4 — Equitable Relief
22	Each Partner acknowledges and agrees that a breach of the confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article XIV may cause irreparable harm to the Partnership, the General Partner, the other Partners, or one or more Portfolio Companies, for which monetary damages may be inadequate. Accordingly, each Partner agrees that, in addition to any other remedies available at law or in equity, the Partnership (and any affected Partner or Portfolio Company) shall be entitled to seek equitable relief, including temporary and permanent injunctive relief and specific performance, to enforce the provisions of this Article XIV, without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting any bond or other security.
23	ARTICLE XV — REPORTING
24	Section 15.1 — Financial Statements
25	The General Partner shall cause to be prepared and delivered to each Limited Partner:
26	(a) Annual Audited Financial Statements. Within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year of the Partnership, audited financial statements of the Partnership for such fiscal year, prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States ("GAAP") and audited by Ironbark Audit Partners LLP (or such other independent accounting firm of recognized national or international standing as the General Partner may select from time to time). The annual audited financial statements shall include a balance sheet, a statement of operations, a statement of changes in partners' capital, a statement of cash flows, and the notes thereto.
27	(b) Quarterly Unaudited Financial Reports. Within sixty (60) days after the end of each calendar quarter (other than the fourth quarter, which shall be covered by the annual audited financial statements), unaudited financial reports of the Partnership, including the information described in Section 15.2.
28	(c) Tax Information. Schedule K-1 (IRS Form 1065) and any other required tax reporting forms to each Partner within seventy-five (75) days after the end of each fiscal year (or such later date as may be permitted for the filing of partnership returns under applicable law), together with such other tax information as may be reasonably necessary for each Partner to prepare its own tax returns. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide estimated tax information to the Partners prior to the due dates for quarterly estimated tax payments.
29	(d) The General Partner shall deliver all financial statements, reports, and other communications to the Limited Partners by electronic delivery (including through a secure investor portal maintained by the Fund Administrator or the Management Company), unless a Limited Partner specifically requests delivery by hard copy.
30	Section 15.2 — Quarterly Reports
31	The quarterly financial reports required by Section 15.1(b) shall include:
32	(a) an unaudited balance sheet and income statement of the Partnership as of the end of such quarter;
33	(b) a summary of all Investments as of the end of such quarter, including the cost basis, fair market value, and unrealized gain or loss for each Investment;
34	(c) a Capital Account statement for each Limited Partner, reflecting the opening balance, Capital Contributions, distributions, allocations of Net Profits and Net Losses, and closing balance for such quarter;
35	(d) a summary of all Capital Calls made and distributions paid during such quarter;
36	(e) a Management Fee calculation and fee offset summary for such quarter; and
37	(f) a summary of material events and developments during such quarter, including any material changes in the financial condition or operations of any Portfolio Company, any material litigation or regulatory matters, and any other information that the General Partner determines to be material to the Limited Partners.
38	The format, content, and level of detail of the quarterly reports may be modified by the General Partner from time to time, consistent with customary industry practice.
39	Section 15.3 — Additional Information
40	The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide the Limited Partners with such additional information as they may reasonably request from time to time in connection with their legal, regulatory, tax, accounting, or reporting obligations, including, without limitation, information required by a Limited Partner to comply with ERISA, applicable tax laws, or the reporting requirements of any governmental authority having jurisdiction over such Limited Partner. The General Partner shall not be obligated to prepare any information not already in its possession or readily obtainable, or to disclose information that the General Partner reasonably believes to be competitively sensitive, proprietary, or the disclosure of which would be harmful to the Partnership, any Portfolio Company, or any other Partner.
41	Section 15.4 — Fund Administrator
42	Ridgeline Trust Company shall serve as the fund administrator for the Partnership. The Fund Administrator shall be responsible for maintaining the Partnership's books and records, calculating the net asset value of the Partnership and each Partner's Capital Account, assisting in the preparation of financial reports and tax returns, processing Capital Calls and distributions, and performing such other administrative functions as the General Partner may direct. The selection and replacement of the Fund Administrator shall be at the discretion of the General Partner.
43	ARTICLE XVI — SIDE LETTERS; MOST FAVORED NATION
44	Section 16.1 — Side Letters Generally
45	As set forth in Section 8.6, the General Partner may enter into Side Letters with one or more Limited Partners that supplement, modify, or waive certain provisions of this Agreement with respect to such Limited Partner(s). Each Side Letter shall form part of this Agreement with respect to the Limited Partner that is a party thereto. In the event of a conflict between the terms of this Agreement and the terms of a Side Letter, the Side Letter shall govern with respect to the Limited Partner that is a party to such Side Letter, but only to the extent of such conflict. The existence and terms of Side Letters shall be subject to disclosure and election in accordance with the MFN provisions set forth in Section 16.2.
46	Section 16.2 — Most Favored Nation Provisions
47	(a) Eligibility. Each Limited Partner that has a Capital Commitment equal to or greater than the MFN Threshold of Seventy-Five Million Dollars ($75,000,000) shall be eligible to receive MFN disclosure and to make MFN Elections in accordance with this Section 16.2.
48	(b) Disclosure Timing. Within fifteen (15) Business Days following the Final Closing, the General Partner shall provide each eligible Limited Partner with copies of (or a summary of the material terms of) all Side Letters entered into by the General Partner with any Limited Partner in connection with the Partnership. Such copies or summaries shall be redacted to remove identifying information regarding the Limited Partner(s) that are parties to each Side Letter.
49	(c) Election Period. Within thirty (30) days following receipt of the Side Letter disclosure described in subsection (b) above, each eligible Limited Partner may make an MFN Election by delivering written notice to the General Partner identifying the specific Side Letter whose terms the electing Limited Partner wishes to receive.
50	(d) Single Side Letter Requirement. Each MFN Election must be made with respect to all of the material terms of a single Side Letter; an electing Limited Partner may not select individual provisions from multiple Side Letters. The purpose of this Single Side Letter Requirement is to preserve the negotiated balance of terms within each Side Letter and to prevent the creation of a composite set of terms that was not agreed upon between the General Partner and any single Limited Partner.
51	(e) Comparability Threshold. An MFN Election may be made only with respect to a Side Letter granted to a Limited Partner whose Capital Commitment does not exceed one hundred fifty percent (150%) of the electing Limited Partner's Capital Commitment.
52	(f) Exclusions. The following provisions shall be excluded from MFN Elections: (i) terms granted solely to address specific legal, tax, or regulatory requirements applicable to a particular Limited Partner; (ii) terms that would, if extended to the electing Limited Partner, increase the obligations or reduce the rights of other Partners or the Partnership; (iii) LPAC membership; and (iv) any terms that the General Partner reasonably determines are not capable of being replicated or extended to additional Limited Partners without material adverse consequences.
53	(g) Effectiveness. Any MFN Election shall become effective ten (10) Business Days following delivery of the election notice to the General Partner.
54	(h) Annual Re-Election. Following each anniversary of the Final Closing, if additional Side Letters have been entered into, the General Partner shall provide updated MFN disclosure to eligible Limited Partners within fifteen (15) Business Days of such anniversary. Each eligible Limited Partner shall have a thirty (30)-day period following receipt of such disclosure to make or modify its MFN Election. Any such updated MFN Election shall be subject to the same requirements and limitations set forth in this Section 16.2, including the Single Side Letter Requirement.
55	ARTICLE XVII — AMENDMENTS; MEETINGS
56	Section 17.1 — Amendments
57	(a) This Agreement may be amended by the General Partner without the consent of the Limited Partners to: (i) cure any ambiguity or correct any error or omission; (ii) reflect the admission, substitution, or withdrawal of Partners; (iii) make changes required by applicable law or regulation; (iv) add provisions for the benefit of the Limited Partners that do not materially and adversely affect the rights of any Limited Partner; or (v) make other changes that do not materially and adversely affect the rights of any Limited Partner.
58	(b) Except as provided in subsection (a) above, any amendment to this Agreement shall require the consent of a Majority in Interest of Limited Partners.
59	(c) Notwithstanding the foregoing, no amendment to this Agreement shall: (i) increase the Capital Commitment of any Partner without the express written consent of such Partner; (ii) reduce the Preferred Return or increase the Carried Interest Percentage without the consent of all Partners adversely affected thereby; (iii) modify the clawback provisions of Section 6.3 in a manner adverse to the Limited Partners without the consent of a Supermajority in Interest (66⅔%) of Limited Partners; or (iv) modify this Section 17.1(c) without the consent of all Partners.
60	(d) Any amendment shall be effective upon (or at such later date as may be specified in) the General Partner's delivery of written notice of such amendment to the Limited Partners, and the General Partner shall provide a copy of any amendment to all Partners within ten (10) Business Days of its effectiveness.
61	Section 17.2 — Meetings of the LPAC
62	(a) The LPAC shall meet at least once per year, and at such additional times as may be determined by the General Partner or upon the written request of a majority of the LPAC members. Meetings shall be convened by the General Partner by delivering written notice to the LPAC members at least fifteen (15) Business Days prior to the date of the meeting, setting forth the date, time, location (or videoconference details), and a reasonably detailed agenda.
63	(b) Meetings of the LPAC may be held in person (at the principal office of the Partnership or at such other location as the General Partner may designate), by telephone conference, by videoconference, or by any combination thereof. Any LPAC member may participate in a meeting by telephone or videoconference, and such participation shall constitute presence in person at such meeting.
64	(c) A quorum for any LPAC meeting shall consist of a majority of the then-serving LPAC members. If a quorum is not present at a scheduled meeting, the meeting may be adjourned by the General Partner to a date and time not less than five (5) Business Days after the originally scheduled date. Notice of any adjourned meeting shall be provided to all LPAC members.
65	(d) The General Partner shall prepare and distribute minutes of each LPAC meeting to all LPAC members within fifteen (15) Business Days of such meeting.
66	Section 17.3 — Voting Rights; Consents
67	Except as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement, all matters requiring the approval or consent of the Limited Partners may be approved by a Majority in Interest of Limited Partners. Consents may be given in writing (including by email) without a meeting, and any consent given in writing shall have the same force and effect as a vote at a duly convened meeting. Each Limited Partner's voting power shall be proportional to such Limited Partner's Capital Commitment relative to the aggregate Capital Commitments of all Limited Partners (excluding the General Partner and any Defaulting Limited Partners). The General Partner shall solicit and tabulate consents and shall provide the results to the Limited Partners within ten (10) Business Days of the expiration of the consent period.
68	ARTICLE XVIII — POWER OF ATTORNEY
69	Section 18.1 — Grant of Power of Attorney
70	Each Limited Partner, by its execution of this Agreement (or a Subscription Agreement incorporating this Agreement by reference), hereby irrevocably appoints the General Partner as its true and lawful attorney-in-fact, with full power of substitution, to act in such Limited Partner's name, place, and stead for the purpose of executing, swearing to, acknowledging, filing, recording, and publishing (a) this Agreement and any amendments hereto, (b) the Certificate of Limited Partnership and any amendments thereto, (c) any certificates, instruments, or documents required to be filed under the laws of the State of Delaware or any other jurisdiction in which the Partnership conducts business, (d) any instruments relating to the admission, substitution, or withdrawal of Partners, and (e) all other instruments, documents, and certificates that may from time to time be required by applicable law to be filed or recorded on behalf of the Partnership. This power of attorney is coupled with an interest and shall survive and shall not be affected by the subsequent dissolution, disability, incapacity, death, or bankruptcy of any Limited Partner. Each Limited Partner hereby agrees to be bound by any representation or action made or taken by the General Partner pursuant to this power of attorney in accordance with the terms of this Agreement.
71	ARTICLE XIX — GOVERNING LAW; DISPUTE RESOLUTION
72	Section 19.1 — Governing Law
73	This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without giving effect to any principles of conflicts of law that would require the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.
74	Section 19.2 — Jurisdiction; Venue
75	Each Partner hereby irrevocably consents and submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of the State of Delaware (including the Delaware Court of Chancery) and the United States District Court for the District of Delaware in connection with any action, suit, or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement. Each Partner waives any objection to venue and any objection based on the doctrine of forum non conveniens. EACH PARTNER HEREBY IRREVOCABLY WAIVES, TO THE FULLEST EXTENT PERMITTED BY APPLICABLE LAW, ANY RIGHT IT MAY HAVE TO A TRIAL BY JURY IN ANY ACTION, SUIT, OR PROCEEDING ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT OR THE TRANSACTIONS CONTEMPLATED HEREBY.
76	Section 19.3 — Arbitration
77	Notwithstanding Section 19.2, any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof, that is not resolved through good-faith negotiation between the parties within thirty (30) days following written notice of such dispute, shall be submitted to final and binding arbitration in New York, New York, administered by JAMS (or such other arbitration organization as the parties may agree) under the commercial arbitration rules then in effect. The arbitration shall be conducted before a panel of three (3) arbitrators, one selected by each party to the dispute and the third selected by agreement of the two party-appointed arbitrators (or, failing agreement, by JAMS). The decision of the arbitrators shall be final, binding, and enforceable in any court of competent jurisdiction. The costs of arbitration shall be allocated by the arbitrators in their award, and each party shall bear its own attorneys' fees and expenses, unless the arbitrators determine that the prevailing party is entitled to an award of reasonable attorneys' fees.
78	ARTICLE XX — MISCELLANEOUS
79	Section 20.1 — Notices
80	All notices, requests, demands, consents, and other communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed to have been duly given or made (a) when delivered by hand or by overnight courier service (such as Federal Express, UPS, or DHL) to the party at the address set forth in Schedule A (or, in the case of the General Partner, at 450 Lexington Avenue, 38th Floor, New York, New York 10017), (b) when sent by email (with written confirmation of receipt by the intended recipient, which may include a read receipt or reply email confirming receipt) to the email address set forth in such party's Subscription Agreement or as otherwise designated in writing, or (c) three (3) Business Days after being sent by registered or certified mail, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, to such address. Any Partner may change its address for notices by delivering written notice of such change to the General Partner (and, in the case of the General Partner, to all Partners) in accordance with this Section 20.1. Notices to the General Partner shall be directed to the attention of the General Counsel, with a copy to Marcus Thornfield, Managing Partner.
81	Section 20.2 — Entire Agreement
82	This Agreement, together with any Side Letters executed in connection herewith, the Subscription Agreements, and the other documents and instruments contemplated hereby, constitutes the entire agreement of the Partners with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior agreements, understandings, negotiations, representations, and warranties, whether written or oral, among the Partners with respect to the subject matter hereof. No Partner has relied on any representation or warranty not set forth in this Agreement.
83	Section 20.3 — Severability
84	If any provision of this Agreement or the application thereof to any Person or circumstance is held by a court of competent jurisdiction or an arbitral tribunal to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the remaining provisions of this Agreement shall continue in full force and effect, and shall not be affected, impaired, or invalidated. The parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace any invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision with a valid provision that, to the greatest extent possible, achieves the economic, business, and other purposes of the invalid provision.
85	Section 20.4 — Successors and Assigns
86	This Agreement shall be binding upon and shall inure to the benefit of the Partners and their respective heirs, executors, administrators, legal representatives, successors, and permitted assigns, in each case subject to and in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement (including the transfer restrictions set forth in Article XII).
87	Section 20.5 — No Third-Party Beneficiaries
88	Nothing in this Agreement, whether express or implied, shall be construed to confer upon any Person other than the Partners and the Indemnified Persons (solely with respect to Article XIII) any rights, remedies, or claims under or by reason of this Agreement or any provision hereof. No creditor of the Partnership or any Partner shall be deemed a third-party beneficiary of this Agreement.
89	Section 20.6 — Counterparts
90	This Agreement may be executed in one or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which, when taken together, shall constitute one and the same instrument. Delivery of an executed counterpart of a signature page to this Agreement by facsimile or electronic transmission (including .pdf format) shall be as effective as delivery of a manually executed counterpart.
91	Section 20.7 — Waiver
92	No waiver of any provision of this Agreement or of any right or remedy hereunder shall be effective unless given in writing and signed by the party granting such waiver. No failure or delay by any party in exercising any right or remedy under this Agreement shall operate as a waiver thereof, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right or remedy preclude any further or other exercise of such right or remedy or any other right or remedy.
93	Section 20.8 — Headings
94	The article, section, and other headings contained in this Agreement are for reference purposes only, are inserted for convenience only, and shall not affect in any way the meaning, construction, or interpretation of this Agreement.
95	Section 20.9 — ERISA Compliance
96	(a) The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that "benefit plan investors" (as defined under Section 3(42) of ERISA and the regulations promulgated by the United States Department of Labor thereunder, including 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101, as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA) hold less than twenty-five percent (25%) of each class of equity interests in the Partnership, such that the assets of the Partnership are not deemed to be "plan assets" under ERISA and the Department of Labor's plan asset regulations. In calculating the twenty-five percent (25%) threshold, the General Partner shall exclude from the denominator any Interest held by the General Partner and its Affiliates, and shall include in the numerator the Interests held by (i) "employee benefit plans" as defined in Section 3(3) of ERISA that are subject to Title I of ERISA, (ii) "plans" as described in Section 4975(e)(1) of the Code that are subject to Section 4975 of the Code, and (iii) entities whose underlying assets include "plan assets" by reason of such entities' investments in the Partnership.
97	(b) Each Limited Partner shall promptly notify the General Partner of any change in its ERISA status, including any change that would cause such Limited Partner to become (or to cease being) a "benefit plan investor" for purposes of this Section 20.9. Each Limited Partner represents that the information provided in its Subscription Agreement regarding its ERISA status is true and correct as of the date of its admission to the Partnership.
98	(c) The General Partner may refuse to admit, or may require the withdrawal or transfer of the Interest of, any Limited Partner if the General Partner determines, in its reasonable discretion, that such admission or continued participation would cause the Partnership's assets to become "plan assets" under ERISA or would otherwise cause the Partnership or the General Partner to be subject to the requirements of Title I of ERISA or Section 4975 of the Code. If the General Partner requires the withdrawal or transfer of a Limited Partner's Interest pursuant to this subsection, such withdrawal or transfer shall be effected on terms that are as equitable as practicable, as determined by the General Partner in good faith.
99	(d) The General Partner shall monitor compliance with the benefit plan investor threshold on an ongoing basis, and shall report to the LPAC at least annually on the percentage of Interests held by benefit plan investors. The General Partner shall not knowingly take any action that would cause the benefit plan investor threshold to be exceeded.
100	[SIGNATURE PAGES FOLLOW]

24	Thornfield Capital Partners LLC as General Partner of Thornfield Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. 450 Lexington Avenue, 38th Floor New York, New York 10017
25	Re: Side Letter Agreement — Meridian State Teachers' Retirement System
26	Ladies and Gentlemen:
27	This Side Letter Agreement (this "Side Letter") is entered into as of the date set forth above, by and between Thornfield Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the "General Partner"), in its capacity as the general partner of Thornfield Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P., a Delaware limited partnership (the "Fund"), and Meridian State Teachers' Retirement System, a public pension fund established under the laws of the State of Meridian (the "Limited Partner" or "Meridian STRS").
28	The Limited Partner proposes to make a Capital Commitment to the Fund in the amount of $125,000,000 (One Hundred Twenty-Five Million Dollars), subject to the terms and conditions of the Fund's Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership dated as of March 15, 2025, as it may be amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time (the "Partnership Agreement" or "LPA"), and this Side Letter.
29	This Side Letter is intended to supplement and modify certain provisions of the Partnership Agreement as applied to the Limited Partner. The terms and conditions set forth herein are in addition to, and not in limitation of, the rights and obligations of the parties under the Partnership Agreement, except to the extent expressly provided herein.
30	RECITALS
31	WHEREAS, the Fund was formed as a Delaware limited partnership pursuant to its Certificate of Limited Partnership filed with the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on January 14, 2025;
32	WHEREAS, the General Partner has delivered to the Limited Partner the Partnership Agreement, the Subscription Agreement, the Confidential Private Placement Memorandum dated February 28, 2025, and related offering documents (collectively, the "Offering Documents");
33	WHEREAS, the Limited Partner proposes to make a Capital Commitment to the Fund of $125,000,000, subject to the terms and conditions of the Partnership Agreement and this Side Letter;
34	WHEREAS, the Limited Partner's Board of Trustees has authorized such commitment pursuant to Resolution 2025-017, adopted at a duly convened meeting of the Board of Trustees held on March 28, 2025;
35	WHEREAS, the Limited Partner is a public pension fund established under the laws of the State of Meridian and is subject to certain statutory and regulatory requirements, including the Meridian Public Retirement System Transparency Act, Meridian Revised Statutes §§ 24-51-201 through 24-51-215 (as amended, the "MPRSTA"), and the Meridian Open Records Act, Meridian Revised Statutes §§ 24-72-100 through 24-72-125 (as amended, the "MORA"), which impose obligations upon the Limited Partner with respect to, among other things, the disclosure of investment information, the transparency of investment fees and expenses, and the public availability of certain records relating to the Limited Partner's investment activities;
36	WHEREAS, the parties desire to supplement the Partnership Agreement with respect to certain matters applicable to the Limited Partner's investment in the Fund, including matters relating to confidentiality, reporting, co-investment, excuse rights, fee arrangements, and other governance matters; and
37	NOW, THEREFORE, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties agree as follows:
38	Section 1 — Definitions; Interpretation
39	1.1 Capitalized terms used but not otherwise defined in this Side Letter shall have the meanings ascribed to such terms in the Partnership Agreement. All references to "dollars" or "$" shall mean United States dollars.
40	1.2 In the event of any conflict or inconsistency between the terms of this Side Letter and the Partnership Agreement, the terms of this Side Letter shall control and prevail with respect to the Limited Partner and the Limited Partner's interest in the Fund. To the extent that any provision of the Partnership Agreement imposes an obligation on the Limited Partner or limits a right of the Limited Partner, and such obligation or limitation is inconsistent with a provision of this Side Letter, the provision of this Side Letter shall govern.
41	1.3 References herein to "Sections" are to sections of this Side Letter unless otherwise indicated. References to sections of the Partnership Agreement shall be designated as "LPA Section [X]." References to any statute or regulation shall be deemed to include any successor statute, regulation, or amendment thereto.
42	Section 2 — Most Favored Nation Rights
43	2.1 MFN Disclosure. The General Partner shall, within fifteen (15) Business Days following the Final Close of the Fund, provide to the Limited Partner complete and unredacted copies of all side letters, supplemental agreements, letter agreements, or other written arrangements entered into between the General Partner (or any of its Affiliates, including the Fund) and any other Limited Partner of the Fund or any Affiliate of any other Limited Partner (each, an "Other LP Side Letter"), together with a summary table prepared by the General Partner identifying each material provision contained in each Other LP Side Letter and the identity of the applicable Limited Partner to which such Other LP Side Letter relates. The summary table shall be organized by subject matter category (including, without limitation, economic terms, governance terms, reporting and information rights, co-investment rights, excuse and exclusion rights, transfer provisions, and other material terms) to facilitate the Limited Partner's review and comparison of such provisions.
44	2.2 MFN Election Right. The Limited Partner shall have the right, exercisable by written notice delivered to the General Partner within thirty (30) calendar days following receipt of the complete disclosure described in Section 2.1 (the "MFN Election Period"), to elect to receive the benefit of any term or provision contained in any Other LP Side Letter that is more favorable to such other Limited Partner than the corresponding term or provision applicable to the Limited Partner under this Side Letter or the Partnership Agreement (each, a "Favorable Provision"). Upon timely exercise of the MFN election right by the Limited Partner, each elected Favorable Provision shall be deemed incorporated into this Side Letter, with all necessary conforming changes, as if originally set forth herein, effective as of the date of the Limited Partner's admission to the Fund.
45	2.3 Provision-by-Provision Election. The Limited Partner's MFN election right under Section 2.2 may be exercised on a provision-by-provision basis, and the Limited Partner shall not be required to elect all provisions from a single Other LP Side Letter or to accept any Favorable Provision as a condition to electing any other Favorable Provision. The Limited Partner may select individual Favorable Provisions from multiple Other LP Side Letters, and each such elected provision shall be incorporated into this Side Letter independently of any other provision contained in the same or any other Other LP Side Letter. For the avoidance of doubt, the Limited Partner may elect any combination of Favorable Provisions from any number of Other LP Side Letters, without limitation as to the number of provisions elected or the number of Other LP Side Letters from which such provisions are drawn, and the General Partner shall not impose any restriction, cap, or other limitation on the number or nature of Favorable Provisions that the Limited Partner may elect.
46	2.4 Ongoing MFN. If at any time after the Final Close the General Partner enters into any new side letter, supplemental agreement, or amended or restated side letter with any Limited Partner of the Fund (or any Affiliate thereof), the General Partner shall promptly (and in any event within ten (10) Business Days of the execution thereof) provide a complete and unredacted copy thereof to the Limited Partner, together with a summary of the material provisions contained therein. The Limited Partner shall have an additional thirty (30) calendar days from receipt of such copy and summary to exercise MFN election rights with respect to any Favorable Provisions contained in such new or amended side letter, on the same terms and subject to the same conditions as set forth in Sections 2.2 and 2.3.
47	2.5 MFN Scope. The MFN election right set forth in this Section 2 shall apply to all terms and provisions contained in any Other LP Side Letter, including without limitation: (a) economic terms, including management fee rates, management fee offsets, management fee bases, carried interest percentages, preferred return rates, catch-up provisions, and hurdle rates; (b) governance terms, including LPAC representation, consent rights, voting thresholds, and removal provisions; (c) reporting and disclosure terms, including the frequency, content, and format of reports; (d) co-investment rights, including rights of first offer, pro-rata participation rights, fee and carry terms applicable to co-investments, and co-investment allocation policies; (e) excuse and exclusion rights; (f) transfer and redemption provisions; (g) key person provisions; (h) clawback and escrow provisions; and (i) any other terms or provisions, regardless of subject matter. The determination of whether a provision constitutes a Favorable Provision shall be made in the reasonable judgment of the Limited Partner.
48	Section 3 — Confidentiality and Public Records / FOIA Carve-Out
49	3.1 Acknowledgment. The General Partner acknowledges and agrees that the Limited Partner is a public pension fund of the State of Meridian and is subject to the Meridian Open Records Act, Meridian Revised Statutes §§ 24-72-100 through 24-72-125, as amended (the "MORA"), and the Meridian Public Retirement System Transparency Act, Meridian Revised Statutes §§ 24-51-201 through 24-51-215, as amended (the "MPRSTA"), and various other applicable public records, open meetings, freedom of information, and transparency laws, regulations, and policies of the State of Meridian, as each may be amended, supplemented, or superseded from time to time (collectively, with MORA and MPRSTA, "Applicable Public Records Laws"). The General Partner further acknowledges that the Limited Partner has a legal obligation to comply with Applicable Public Records Laws, and that such compliance may require the disclosure of information that would otherwise be treated as confidential under the Partnership Agreement.
50	3.2 FOIA/Public Records Carve-Out. Notwithstanding LPA Section 12.1 or any other provision of the Partnership Agreement, this Side Letter, the Subscription Agreement, the Confidential Private Placement Memorandum, or any other agreement, arrangement, or understanding between the parties (whether written or oral), the Limited Partner shall be permitted to disclose any and all information relating to the Fund, the General Partner, or any of their respective Affiliates, including without limitation the Partnership Agreement (and all amendments, supplements, and side letters thereto), this Side Letter, the Limited Partner's Capital Commitment, the Capital Commitments of other Limited Partners, Capital Account balances, management fee and carried interest calculations, fund-level and portfolio-level expense information, gross and net performance data (including internal rates of return, multiples, and benchmark comparisons), portfolio company information (including the identity, industry, geographic location, acquisition cost, and current valuation of each portfolio company), co-investor identities and co-investment amounts, valuation data, methodologies and supporting analyses, the identity of the Fund's auditor and other service providers, and any other information relating to the Fund, the General Partner, any Affiliate of the General Partner, or any portfolio company or investment of the Fund (collectively, "Fund Information"), to the extent that the Limited Partner determines, in its sole discretion, that such disclosure is required, requested, or appropriate pursuant to Applicable Public Records Laws, including in response to any request made under MORA, MPRSTA, or any other applicable statute or regulation, or pursuant to any subpoena, civil investigative demand, legislative inquiry, audit request, or similar legal or regulatory process.
51	3.3 No Prior Consent or Notice Required. The Limited Partner shall not be required to (a) provide advance notice to the General Partner prior to making any disclosure pursuant to Section 3.2, (b) obtain the prior written or oral consent of the General Partner for any such disclosure, (c) seek confidential treatment, proprietary treatment, or protective treatment of any Fund Information prior to disclosure, (d) designate or request the designation of any Fund Information as exempt from disclosure under any Applicable Public Records Law, or (e) afford the General Partner any opportunity to review, challenge, contest, appeal, or seek to prevent or delay such disclosure, whether through judicial proceedings, administrative proceedings, or otherwise. For the avoidance of doubt, the General Partner shall have no right to seek injunctive relief, temporary restraining orders, or any other form of equitable or legal relief to prevent, delay, or modify any disclosure made by the Limited Partner in good faith under Section 3.2, and the General Partner hereby irrevocably waives any right to seek such relief.
52	3.4 No Breach. Any disclosure made by the Limited Partner pursuant to Section 3.2 shall not constitute a breach of the confidentiality provisions of the Partnership Agreement, this Side Letter, or any other agreement between the parties, and the Limited Partner shall not be liable to the General Partner, the Fund, any other Limited Partner, or any other Person for any damages (whether direct, indirect, consequential, incidental, special, or punitive), losses, claims, costs, or expenses arising from or relating to such disclosure. The General Partner shall not assert, and hereby waives, any claim against the Limited Partner arising from any disclosure made by the Limited Partner in good faith pursuant to Section 3.2.
53	3.5 Cooperation. The General Partner shall cooperate with the Limited Partner and provide such information and assistance as the Limited Partner may reasonably request in connection with the Limited Partner's compliance with Applicable Public Records Laws, including by providing information in such formats as the Limited Partner may reasonably request (including electronic and machine-readable formats), responding to requests for clarification or supplemental information within five (5) Business Days, and assisting the Limited Partner in preparing any required filings, reports, or disclosures. Such cooperation shall be provided at no additional cost to the Limited Partner or the Fund.
54	Section 4 — Regulatory Disclosure and Reporting
55	4.1 MPRSTA Compliance. The General Partner acknowledges that the Limited Partner is required to disclose certain information pursuant to MPRSTA on a semi-annual basis within ninety (90) days of each period end (i.e., within ninety (90) days of June 30 and December 31 of each year). The information required to be disclosed includes: (a) all management fees and advisory fees paid by the Limited Partner or charged to the Fund that are attributable to the Limited Partner's interest; (b) carried interest allocations, incentive compensation, and performance data attributable to the Limited Partner's interest in the Fund, including gross and net internal rates of return, investment multiples, and benchmark comparisons; (c) all fund-level expenses and organizational expenses charged to the Fund or the Limited Partner, including legal fees, audit fees, travel expenses, broken deal expenses, and any other expenses borne by the Fund; and (d) all placement agent, finder, solicitor, and intermediary fees, compensation, and relationships applicable to the Fund. The General Partner shall provide such information to the Limited Partner in a format and with sufficient detail to enable the Limited Partner to comply with its obligations under MPRSTA, and shall deliver such information to the Limited Partner no later than sixty (60) days after each semi-annual period end to allow the Limited Partner reasonable time for review and preparation of its required filings.
56	4.2 Placement Agent Disclosure. The General Partner represents, warrants, and covenants as follows with respect to placement agents:
57	(a) The General Partner shall disclose to the Limited Partner the identity of each placement agent, finder, solicitor, marketing consultant, or other intermediary (each, a "Placement Agent") retained, engaged, or utilized by the General Partner, the Fund, or any of their respective Affiliates in connection with the offer, sale, marketing, or distribution of interests in the Fund, including the name, address, and principal place of business of each Placement Agent, the date of engagement, and the scope of services provided.
58	(b) The General Partner shall disclose to the Limited Partner all fees, commissions, compensation, and other consideration (whether in the form of cash, equity interests, carried interest participations, expense reimbursements, or otherwise) paid, payable, or expected to be paid to each Placement Agent, including (i) the fee percentage or fee schedule applicable to each Placement Agent, (ii) the aggregate dollar amount of fees paid or expected to be paid to each Placement Agent over the life of the Fund (including any ongoing or trailing compensation), and (iii) the source of payment for such fees, specifying whether such fees are borne by the Fund (and therefore by the Limited Partners), by the General Partner or its Affiliates out of the management fee or other General Partner revenues, or by some combination thereof.
59	(c) The General Partner shall disclose to the Limited Partner the identities of all Limited Partners whose Capital Commitments were introduced, solicited, or otherwise procured, in whole or in part, by each Placement Agent, together with the Capital Commitment amount attributable to each such Limited Partner. If any Placement Agent was involved in the solicitation of Capital Commitments from multiple Limited Partners, the General Partner shall identify each such Limited Partner and the corresponding Capital Commitment amount separately.
60	(d) The General Partner shall provide the disclosures described in this Section 4.2 within thirty (30) days of the date of this Side Letter and shall update such disclosures within fifteen (15) Business Days following each subsequent closing of the Fund and, thereafter, within fifteen (15) Business Days of any material change in the information previously disclosed.
61	(e) The General Partner represents and warrants that no Placement Agent was involved in the introduction, solicitation, or procurement of the Limited Partner's Capital Commitment to the Fund, and that no placement fees, solicitation fees, finder's fees, or other compensation of any kind are payable to any Person in connection with the Limited Partner's Capital Commitment. The General Partner agrees to indemnify and hold harmless the Limited Partner from and against any claim for fees, commissions, or other compensation asserted by any Person claiming to have acted as a Placement Agent or intermediary in connection with the Limited Partner's Capital Commitment.
62	4.3 Regulatory Reporting Assistance. The General Partner shall provide to the Limited Partner, upon reasonable request and without undue delay, such additional information, data, and supporting documentation as may be necessary or appropriate for the Limited Partner to comply with any reporting, filing, or disclosure obligations imposed by any governmental authority, regulatory body, legislative body, or self-regulatory organization having jurisdiction over the Limited Partner, including without limitation the State of Meridian, any agency or instrumentality thereof, MPRSTA, MORA, and any successor or amendatory legislation. Such information shall be provided at no additional cost to the Limited Partner and in such format (including electronic formats) as the Limited Partner may reasonably request.
63	4.4 Third-Party Auditor Access. The Limited Partner and its authorized representatives, including the State of Meridian Auditor's Office, the Meridian Legislative Audit Committee, and any independent auditor retained by the Limited Partner, shall have the right, upon reasonable prior notice (not to exceed ten (10) Business Days) and during normal business hours, to inspect, audit, examine, and copy the books, records, and accounts of the Fund and the General Partner relating to the Limited Partner's interest in the Fund, the calculation and payment of management fees and carried interest, fund-level expenses, and any other matters material to the Limited Partner's investment. The General Partner shall make appropriate personnel available to assist in any such inspection or audit.
64	Section 5 — Reporting and Information Rights
65	5.1 Quarterly Reports. The General Partner shall provide to the Limited Partner, within sixty (60) days after the end of each fiscal quarter of the Fund, the following reports and information:
66	(a) unaudited financial statements of the Fund, including a balance sheet as of the end of such quarter, an income statement for such quarter and for the year-to-date period, and a statement of cash flows for such quarter and for the year-to-date period, in each case prepared in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States;
67	(b) a portfolio company summary for each investment held by the Fund as of the end of such quarter, including a description of the investment (including the nature of the securities held, the industry and geographic location of the portfolio company, and the date of initial investment), the aggregate cost basis, the estimated fair market value as of the end of such quarter, the basis for such valuation, and a brief narrative update on material developments affecting each portfolio company, including any material changes in operating performance, management, capital structure, or market conditions;
68	(c) a capital account statement for the Limited Partner reflecting all capital contributions made, all distributions received, all allocations of income, gain, loss, deduction, and expense, all management fees and other charges, and the ending capital account balance as of the end of such quarter; and
69	(d) a schedule of all fees and expenses charged to the Fund during such quarter, including management fees, organizational expenses, operating expenses, legal fees, audit fees, custody fees, transaction fees, monitoring fees, director fees, and any other fees or expenses of any nature, together with a reasonably detailed description of each such fee or expense.
70	5.2 Annual Audited Financial Statements. The General Partner shall cause audited financial statements of the Fund to be prepared by Ironbark Audit Partners LLP (or such other independent accounting firm of national reputation as may be selected by the General Partner) in accordance with generally accepted accounting principles in the United States, and delivered to the Limited Partner within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year of the Fund. Such audited financial statements shall include the auditor's opinion letter, a balance sheet, an income statement, a statement of cash flows, a statement of changes in partners' capital, and notes to the financial statements, all in reasonable detail.
71	5.3 Tax Information. The General Partner shall provide estimated tax information, including a draft Schedule K-1 (IRS Form 1065) or equivalent, to the Limited Partner within seventy-five (75) days after the end of each fiscal year of the Fund, and final tax information, including the final Schedule K-1, within one hundred twenty (120) days after the end of each fiscal year. The General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to provide the Limited Partner with advance notice of any material items of income, gain, loss, or deduction expected to be allocated to the Limited Partner that may affect the Limited Partner's tax reporting or financial statements.
72	5.4 ESG Reporting. The General Partner shall provide to the Limited Partner, on an annual basis (concurrent with the delivery of the audited financial statements), a report regarding the Fund's environmental, social, and governance ("ESG") policies and practices, including a description of any ESG policy or framework adopted by the General Partner or the Fund, a summary of any ESG-related due diligence or screening conducted with respect to prospective portfolio company investments, a summary of any ESG-related monitoring or engagement activities conducted with respect to existing portfolio companies, and a description of any material ESG risks or incidents identified during the reporting period. The General Partner shall also report on any portfolio company involvement in industries or activities identified on the Limited Partner's restricted investment list, as described in Section 8.
73	5.5 Annual Meeting. The General Partner shall convene an annual in-person meeting of all Limited Partners of the Fund (the "Annual Meeting"), to be held at a location reasonably determined by the General Partner (with consideration given to the geographic convenience of the Fund's largest Limited Partners), at which the General Partner shall present the audited financial statements, a comprehensive portfolio review (including updates on each portfolio company investment), a market outlook, an overview of the Fund's pipeline and investment strategy, and an opportunity for questions, discussion, and dialogue between the Limited Partners and the General Partner's investment professionals. Such Annual Meeting shall be held no later than one hundred eighty (180) days after the end of each fiscal year of the Fund. The General Partner shall provide the Limited Partner with not less than thirty (30) days' advance written notice of each Annual Meeting, together with an agenda and any materials to be presented.
74	Section 6 — LPAC Seat
75	6.1 Advisory Committee Appointment. The General Partner shall appoint the Limited Partner (or its designated representative) as a member of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee of the Fund (the "LPAC") for the full term of the Fund, including any extensions thereof. Such appointment shall be effective as of the date of the Limited Partner's admission to the Fund and shall continue until the dissolution and final winding up of the Fund's affairs.
76	6.2 LPAC Rights. The Limited Partner's representative on the LPAC shall have all rights and privileges accorded to LPAC members under the Partnership Agreement, including without limitation the right to receive advance notice of and participate in all LPAC meetings (whether in person, by teleconference, or by videoconference), the right to vote on all matters submitted to the LPAC for approval or review (including conflicts of interest, valuation determinations, and related-party transactions), and access to all information, materials, and reports provided to the LPAC by the General Partner.
77	6.3 Designated Representative. The Limited Partner's initial designated representative on the LPAC shall be James Teague, Deputy CIO – Private Markets, or such other individual as the Limited Partner may designate from time to time by written notice to the General Partner. The Limited Partner shall have the right to appoint an alternate representative to attend any LPAC meeting in the absence of the primary designated representative, upon written notice to the General Partner.
78	6.4 No Removal Without Consent. The Limited Partner's LPAC seat shall not be revoked, suspended, or terminated by the General Partner without the prior written consent of the Limited Partner, so long as the Limited Partner maintains a Capital Commitment to the Fund of at least $75,000,000 (whether funded or unfunded). In the event that the Limited Partner's Capital Commitment is reduced below $75,000,000 as a result of transfers permitted under Section 10, the General Partner and the Limited Partner shall discuss in good faith whether continued LPAC membership is appropriate under the circumstances.
79	Section 7 — Co-Investment Rights
80	7.1 Right of First Offer. The General Partner shall, prior to offering any co-investment opportunity to any other Person (including any other Limited Partner of the Fund, any Affiliate of the General Partner, any employee or principal of the General Partner, or any third party), first offer such co-investment opportunity to the Limited
